en: Points of Controversy The Great Fifty-Section The Thirteenth Chapter
The Discourse on the Attainment of the Wholesome:
Could one who is a worldling (kappaṭṭha) not attain a wholesome state of consciousness?
Yes, he could.
“Would a worldling (kappaṭṭha) give a gift?”—Yes.
If indeed a worldling could give a gift, then surely it should not be said: [that he cannot].
“An one who has stood for an eon would not obtain a wholesome state of mind.
An one who has stood for an eon would not obtain a wholesome state of mind? Yes.
A worldling might give a robe … [and so on] … might give almsfood … [and so on] … might give a lodging … [and so on].
One should give medicinal requisites for the support of the sick;
one should give food to be chewed;
one should give food to be eaten.
One should give water...
one should pay homage to a shrine...
one should offer a garland at a shrine...
Would one offer incense...
would one offer ointment...
and so forth... or perform a circumambulation of the shrine?
“Yes.
“If a world-endurer were to perform a circumambulation of a shrine,
surely it should not be said that ‘a world-enduler does not obtain a wholesome state of mind’ … [and so on] …”
“Could one who is a worldling (kappaṭṭha) obtain a wholesome state of consciousness?”—
“Yes.”—
“Then could he obtain a wholesome state of consciousness upon emerging from that [attainment]?”
Yes. [It is] the fine-material sphere …pe… the immaterial sphere …pe…
"Could one obtain supramundane wholesome consciousness?
"One should not say so... [and so on].
The Discussion on the Attainment of the Wholesome is finished.
